raw_response:
The raw_merchants table has 46 rows for 40 distinct merchant_ids. Six ids appear twice, and the copies are identical in every column. The join in gold_mcc_daily therefore fans out and inflates the count from 4699 to 5416.

The fix is to deduplicate in silver_merchants. Using SELECT DISTINCT on merchant_id and mcc is safe because the duplicates are fully identical. The distinct counts show 40 merchant_ids, and the mcc values are consistent across copies.

I considered whether the duplicates could differ in some other way. The report says none of the columns differ, so DISTINCT collapses them exactly. If a merchant_id had two different mcc values, DISTINCT would still leave two rows, but the report rules that out.

The other tables are not affected. gold_merchant_daily and gold_customer_spend do not use merchants, and the customers table has no duplicates.
